name: Henry Aldrich
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Henry Aldrich (1648–1710) was an English scholar, logician and amateur architect and composer. He became Dean of Christ Church, Oxford, in 1689 and is remembered for his Artis logicae compendium and for a set of Latin and English verses on the five reasons for drinking.

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: Reasons for Drinking
poems.author: Henry Aldrich
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
If all be true that I do think,
There are five reasons we should drink;
Good wine — a friend — or being dry—
Or lest we should be by and by—
Or any other reason why.
